tasks.instruction: An entry stored at time p0 and checked at time p1 (the clock wraps around) must count as expired as soon as the elapsed time reaches the time-to-live p2, not only once it exceeds it.
tasks.note: Boundary at elapsed == ttl; wrapped clock case; wrong edit also reverses the subtraction.

tasks.instruction: The field read from p0 starting at bit p1 is four bits wide, not three; keep the rest of the computation (field times ten plus p2, limited to 99) as it is.
tasks.note: Mask constant changed from 7 to 15 in the middle of a 6-statement function; wrong edit uses 16.

tasks.instruction: Free shipping should start at a discounted price of 40 instead of 50: prices below 40 still pay the 5 shipping charge, 40 and above pay none.
tasks.note: Constant in the middle of an 8-statement function; wrong edit makes 40 itself pay shipping.

tasks.instruction: The bucket number should keep the low 12 bits of the mixed value instead of the low 10 bits.
tasks.note: Mask constant changed in the last statement of a 7-statement mixing function.

tasks.instruction: Halve the element at the position given by the second argument (positions wrap around the array); the function currently halves the element after it.
tasks.note: Array update index; wrong edit reads the right slot but writes the next one.

tasks.instruction: The total should include all four elements of the array; it currently leaves out the last one.
tasks.note: Fold count over an array; wrong edit runs past the end and wraps to the first element again.

tasks.instruction: Requested bits p0 are allowed only when the request is non-empty and every requested bit is granted in p1 and not revoked in p2; fix the bit operation that combines the request with the effective grants.
tasks.note: One bitwise op changed mid-function; wrong edit ignores the revoked mask.

tasks.instruction: The helper weighs its first argument three times; f should pass p0 as that weighted argument and p1 as the second, then subtract p1 plus one as before.
tasks.note: Swapped call arguments; wrong edit passes p0 twice.

tasks.instruction: Shift the array toward the front instead of toward the back: position i should take the element from position i+1, and the last position takes the fill value p1.
tasks.note: Every element of the built array changes; wrong edit rotates the first element to the end.

tasks.instruction: Apply the discount p1 before tax: the net price is p0 minus p1 (but never below zero), and the result is the net price plus the tax on the net price.
tasks.note: Several statements added; wrong edit taxes the gross price.

tasks.instruction: Return (remaining, exhausted) for usage p0 against limit p1: remaining must be zero once usage reaches or passes the limit, and exhausted must be true as soon as usage reaches the limit.
tasks.note: Two nodes change (flag comparison and a zeroing select); wrong edit fixes only the remaining.

tasks.instruction: Change the scaling from three halves to five quarters of p0 (multiply first, then divide), and add one to the result.
tasks.note: Two constants and an added statement; wrong edits drop the +1 or divide before multiplying.

tasks.instruction: The function should return the length of the run of equal values at the start of the array (how many leading elements equal the first one, stopping at the first different element); today a later match after a mismatch still extends the count.
tasks.note: Reader must see the counts are not chained; wrong edit chains the last step to the wrong predecessor.

tasks.instruction: Given a weekday p0 between 0 and 6 and a number of days p1, return the weekday (0 to 6) reached after moving p1 days forward; at the moment the result is never 6.
tasks.note: Modulus 6 to 7; reference reduces p1 first so huge offsets do not wrap; wrong edits forget the final reduction or let the sum wrap.

tasks.instruction: The function should be true exactly when one of the three flags is true; it currently also returns true when all three are true.
tasks.note: Odd parity of three bools is not exactly-one; all eight combinations tested.

tasks.instruction: The function should return the largest rise from one element to the next element within the array; it must not treat the first element as following the last one.
tasks.note: The helper wraps the index, so a count of four compares last to first; wrong edit skips the final pair.
